cr_arrows_south.description:
I'm Ruka, the quartermaster. You're not in my ledger, which means you're free, which means you can carry.

The road south to Camp Taurajo runs between two quilboar holds, Bramblescar on one side and Agama'gor on the other. There's one ranger on it, a tauren called Kishi, and she's been holding that road with a bow and a bad temper since the season turned.

She sent word she's down to her last quiver. I can't send a patrol, but I can send arrows. Don't tell her they're from me, or she'll want to argue about the fletching.
cr_arrows_south.accept_text: South gate, then straight down the Taurajo road. It's a long walk, most of the way to the camp. Kishi stands on the road itself, where the thorn closes in on both sides.
cr_arrows_south.turn_in_text:
These arrows came from the Crossroads. Let me guess: Ruka, and she told you not to say.

The fletching's crooked. It always is, and I'll use every one.

Since you've walked this far, the thorn on both sides of this road is full of quilboar, and I've got a list.

cr_board_dreadmist.description:
I'm Grukan, and I keep the board. You're looking at the bottom of it, which is where the old ones go.

That one's been up since before the last rains. The Burning Blade has a den on Dreadmist Peak, north-west of here, and somebody posted coin for it. Others have taken the notice down before you. None of them put it back, and none of them collected.

There's a scout up there now, Zarla Blackthorn, who went to find out what happened to them. She's still reporting, so she's still alive, and that makes her the only one who knows the ground. Take her the notice. If the bounty's ever paid, it'll be on her say.
cr_board_dreadmist.accept_text: South gate, then north-west. It's a long way, past the Forgotten Pools, to where the ground climbs toward Dreadmist Peak. Zarla's camp is in the rocks below the canyon mouth. Keep your voice down when you get there.
cr_board_dreadmist.turn_in_text:
Keep your voice down. Quieter than that.

Let me see. Oh, that old thing. Grukan still has it up? There are names on the back, and I've found most of them.

If you want to collect on this, you do it my way, and my way starts with not being heard.

cr_crossroads_holds.description:
You, come here. I've been counting.

When you first walked through my gate, I had the Kolkar building a war camp east of me, quilboar closing the Taurajo road to the south, and the oases going bad to the south-west. That was three fires, and one town in the middle with no soldiers to send to any of them.

Dorn's last report says the warbringer is dead. Kishi's says the wardchief of Bramblescar is dead. And Sanu, who never sends anyone, sent a runner to say the queen under Lushwater is dead and the springs are running clean. I didn't do any of that. I sat behind this wall and wrote orders. Sit down and tell me how it was done, because it's going in a report and I intend to get it right.
cr_crossroads_holds.turn_in_text:
That's the east, the south and the water, all three, and I never left the wall.

I'm going to write it exactly as you told it, and I'm going to write that the Crossroads holds. I've written that every month for three years, and this is the first time I've believed it.

Choose something from the armoury. Then I've one more thing to ask, and it isn't an order.

cr_dispatch_orgrimmar.description:
I'm Kol, a runner, and I've got a problem with two legs, both mine.

This goes to Orgrimmar. It's Sergra's count of what the Crossroads is holding and what it can't, and it's meant to be there by nightfall. I've already run it in from the south road this morning, and my left knee has made its position clear.

You're going that way sooner or later, because everyone does. Scout Windrider in the city takes the Barrens reports. He'll want to hear how the road looked too, so keep your eyes open on the way.
cr_dispatch_orgrimmar.accept_text: North-east from the south gate to the Southfury bridge, across into Durotar, then north up the highway to Orgrimmar. Scout Windrider takes the reports in the city. Don't open the case.
cr_dispatch_orgrimmar.turn_in_text:
This is from the Crossroads? You're not Kol.

Don't explain, I can guess. It's the knee. Let me see the seal. It's unbroken, good.

Sergra says she's holding. She always says she's holding. Tell me what the road actually looked like, and then I've got work for someone who's just walked it.

cr_envoys_report.description:
I'm Envoy Thaelis, of Silvermoon, and you'll do.

I'm to report on the Horde's holdings in the Barrens. So far I've reported on this town, which took a paragraph. Silvermoon will want more than a paragraph, and I'm told the rest of it's outdoors.

There are three places I need. The Sentinel Rocks, north of here, where the herders say something has nested. The Kodo Graveyard beyond them, where the great beasts go to die, which I'm assured is a real place and not an orcish joke. And the Forgotten Pools to the north-west, where pilgrims went to pray and didn't come back. Walk to each, look at it, and tell me what the Horde is actually holding.
cr_envoys_report.turn_in_text:
Scorpids in the rocks, a valley of bones with something walking in it, and a pool full of the drowned.

So the Horde holds a town, three roads, and a great deal of ground it hasn't yet asked permission to stand on. That's more honest than I expected, and I shall report it as such.

Silvermoon is grateful. Take something from the envoy's chest.

cr_hale_letter.description:
I'm Corwin Hale, and I drive for the caravans. You'll have noticed I'm not an orc.

There's a woman in Ratchet called Delia Thorne. She's from Stormwind, like me, and she left it, like me. We came over on the same boat and agreed we'd never speak of home again, and we've kept to that for years by not speaking at all.

I've written to her eleven times, as it happens, and this is the first letter I haven't burned. The Ratchet run's stopped. I'd take it myself, but with the whole road to think about it, I'd turn round. Would you take it by hand? She won't take it from a goblin.
cr_hale_letter.accept_text: South gate, then the Ratchet road south-east, all the way to the coast. Delia keeps to the south end of town, away from the docks.
cr_hale_letter.turn_in_text:
This is from Corwin Hale? He wrote 'by hand' on it. Of course he did. Twelve years, and he still thinks I'd lose a letter.

Give me a moment, and don't go yet. If you're going back that way, I may need you to carry something that isn't a letter, and isn't short.

cr_one_careful_owner.description:
Snix Cogsworth, purveyor of luck, at your service! You look like someone with legs.

Here's the thing. I sell luck. Mostly it's charms, a plainstrider feather on a bit of cord, blessed by a shaman, or by somebody standing near a shaman. I used to be unable to keep them on the table. A caravan driver would buy three.

Then your lot showed up, people who get killed on Tuesday and are back complaining about it on Wednesday. Nobody buys luck from me any more. Why would they? You've made dying look like a bad night's sleep. So I'm doing hats, with feathers in them. Bring me the feathers and I'll cut you in.
cr_one_careful_owner.accept_text: The big plainstriders, out the south gate on the Central Barrens plain. They're everywhere, in every direction. Bring me unbroken feathers. The broken ones look like bad luck, and I've got enough of that.
cr_one_careful_owner.turn_in_text:
They're unbroken, every one of them! Look at the barbs on that.

I hold your whole kind responsible for my margins, and I want that understood. But I've got no quarrel with you personally. Here, the first hat's on the house. I'm charging you double for the second.

cr_orders_east.description:
I'm Sergra Darkthorn, and I command here, so you'll forgive me if I get to it.

The Kolkar hold the plains east of this town. They've had an outpost on the east road for years, and now there's a war camp behind it. A war camp means somebody has decided to stop raiding and start taking.

I've got one watcher on that road, Dorn, on the rise where the grass gives out. He's been asking me for soldiers, and I don't have soldiers. I've got these orders, which tell him to hold where he is and use whoever I send, and that means you. Take them to him, and if he has work, it's my work.
cr_orders_east.accept_text: Out the south gate, which is the only one, then east along the road. Dorn keeps his watch on the rise before the Kolkar Outpost. If you can see their tents, you've passed him.
cr_orders_east.turn_in_text:
Sergra sent these? Give them here.

'Hold where you are and use whoever I send.' Is that all of it? No, that's fair. It's exactly what I'd have written.

So you're who she sent. Let me show you what I've been looking at.

cr_stew_for_sanu.description:
I'm Boorka, and I keep the inn. Don't sit down, I need you standing.

There's a tauren at Lushwater Oasis, Sanu, who keeps the springs. She used to come up to town once a month for a proper meal and the gossip, and she hasn't come in two. The caravan drivers say she won't leave the water now. They say something's wrong with it and she's sitting up nights watching it.

Nobody who sits up nights is eating, so I've made her a crock. Take it down to her. And look at that water while you're there, because if the oases are going bad, this town goes next.
cr_stew_for_sanu.accept_text: South gate, then south-west across the plain to Lushwater Oasis, the big green one. You can't miss the trees. Sanu sits on the east bank.
cr_stew_for_sanu.turn_in_text:
Boorka sent this? Earth Mother keep her. I hadn't noticed I was hungry until I smelled it.

Sit a moment. You've walked a long way to bring an old cow her supper, and I've got something to show you that I'd rather not look at alone.

cr_what_it_costs.description:
I'm Thokk, and you should sit down, because you make the gate look untidy.

You're going north eventually. They all do, up the Gold Road, through the Rampart and into Ashenvale to cut trees the night elves would rather keep. I did it for six years.

There's a captain on the Rampart now, Korvash. They call him Gatebreaker, which tells you he's young. He sends recruits past that wall every week, and I don't believe anyone has told him what's on the other side of it. Ask me about it first. Then take him my tag. He'll know the notches.
cr_what_it_costs.turn_in_text:
Where did you get this? It's a Warsong tally tag, with nine notches and an eye punched through it.

This is One-Eye Thokk's. He's still alive? They told us the whole first line went down at the river. Nobody does nine seasons, and he did.

Tell me what he said to you, all of it, and then I'm going to change some orders.

cr_wheels_for_dogan.description:
I'm Dresk, a caravan guard. I'm meant to be on the Ratchet run today and I'm not, because the Ratchet run isn't running.

Dogan Ironcart's wagons are stopped at Raider's Rest Oasis, on the road south-east. Three of them have lost their axles, and the axles aren't broken, they've been taken. Somebody pulled the pins in the night, which is what bandits do when they'd like you to stay put while they fetch their friends.

I've got spare pins, and I've also got orders not to leave the gate. You haven't, so take them to him.
cr_wheels_for_dogan.accept_text: South gate, then south-east along the Ratchet road until you see water and wagons. That's Raider's Rest. Dogan is the goblin shouting at the wagons.
cr_wheels_for_dogan.turn_in_text:
Pins, at last! Do you know what it costs me per day to sit here? I know exactly, because I've been counting, and it's the only thing keeping me warm.

Dresk sent you? Then you can fight, and that's good, because the people who took these are still here and I'd like to discuss it with them.

cr_word_for_the_tribes.description:
Orgrimmar gets a copy of this. Orgrimmar gets a copy of everything.

The other copy is for Camp Taurajo. The tauren lost their city and they lost Cairne, and since then every piece of news that's gone down that road has been bad: another herd gone, another well soured, another camp that stopped answering. Elder Longtread carries all of it. I've met him, and he doesn't complain, which is how you know.

I want him to hear this from someone who was there, not from a runner. And when you've told him, ask him what the south looks like. The road's open now, and I expect I'm about to find out what was on the other end of it.
cr_word_for_the_tribes.turn_in_text:
This is from Sergra Darkthorn? Read it to me, because my eyes aren't what they were.

'The Crossroads holds.' I haven't had a letter that began well since the bluffs fell. I'm going to have it read out at the fire tonight, and I'm going to have it read twice.

You were there. Then sit, and eat, and afterwards I'll tell you what lies south of this camp, because the road you opened doesn't end here.
